candidates.rationale: First: directly checked approval/recovery architecture and prospective procurement timing; must establish supplier evidence, exact hold, independent review and useful activity.
Second: matched national/coordinated pair with a common host-service alternative that might reduce repeated approvals; exact delegation and evaluator/recipient rights remain open.

Third: packet-reported remediation and bilateral methods provide technical precedent, but actual release rights, Japanese acceptance and net reuse benefit remain missing; baseline primary access weaker.

assumptions: A suitable Gen-nai application and lawful, still-changeable acceptance surface exist before the proposed January2027 feasibility checkpoint.
An authorised owner can control the relevant configuration and credentials without pretending to control upstream worldwide release.
A non-developing reviewer can obtain sufficient evidence within a pre-agreed quote/queue and recurring-update budget; no amount or staffing availability is established.
Manual or restricted-function fallback can maintain the necessary administrative service and correction rights.
Seeded staging faults are informative about this control chain but do not estimate production incidence or harm prevented.

objections.text: Upstream changes, retirement and unavailable proprietary evidence may make Japan's apparent procurement leverage unenforceable in practice.
A common CSC service decision could give LUMI better breadth per unit approval effort than the national-first recommendation assumes.
A real Brazilian failed-assurance case may deserve priority over a prospective test if immediate rights protection is weighted more highly.
A successful local rehearsal could have little additional effect over existing review, consume scarce staff, or displace activity beyond the gate.

unknowns: Japan: actual delegation, signed supplier acceptance/remedy schedule, final tender, selected workflow and model version identity.
Japan: independent-review quote, available staff, queue, update frequency, actual service utility, false holds, correction access and bypass.
LUMI: exact CSC/consortium amendment delegation, national approvals, outside-evaluator permissions, selected recipients and consumed jobs under the condition.
Singapore pair: binding national release owners, second/third recipient acceptance, comparable execution conditions, held-out results and saved total effort.
Brazil: operative technical note, full case record, present disposition, response/receipt dates and independently checked correction.
Finance: discretionary future event and enforceable rights; compute: service-stop versus funding-stop rights and off-platform substitution.
No inspected route demonstrates a complete exact-safeguard authority-to-outcome chain or a comparable causal impact denominator.

Primary-access limits: only four saved source text extracts were inspected; other attributed factual comparisons are secondary packet evidence. The SG/KR refresh403, India contract/AISI403s, SEC raw403 and rights-case missing technical records are not evidence of nonexistence.

validationTest.name: Gen-nai release and forced-retirement rehearsal
validationTest.status: Proposed; no owner agreement, authorisation, spending or execution claimed

prerequisites: Selected useful workflow and synthetic staging data
Costed reviewer availability and recurring-burden cap
Predeclared failure, utility, correction and false-hold thresholds
validationTest.design: Freeze model endpoint/version evidence, application, retrieval data, tool permissions and harness. Blind existing and separate review to clean, seeded-fault and repaired builds. Include tool-side disclosure/unauthorised action and simulated upstream update/retirement. Observe the genuine release pipeline rejecting the faulty build, scoped permission restriction, useful fallback and fresh held-out retest before repaired acceptance. No deliberately unsafe live deployment.
measures: Actual reject/hold/retest decisions and override attempts
Fallback recovery and legitimate work completed
Reviewer-hours, queue time, cash cost and repeat-update burden
In-scope activity ledger and off-gate migration
validationTest.decisionRule: Require the critical seeded defect to be detected and held; require useful-service and burden thresholds agreed before results. If lawful control/evidence is absent or additional protection does not improve current review within those constraints, stop scaling and reconsider the alternatives. An authority failure is a feasibility result, not consent to substitute a mock approval.
validationTest.coverageRule: A staging pass demonstrates feasibility only. Join eventual accepted configuration to actual activity logs before claiming operational coverage; no causal harm-reduction or cross-border-wide control claim.
